subject: geom_text, lm_eqn always showed the last value in a serial of plots

messages.author: eedd19a51dd1e44e
messages.subject: geom_text, lm_eqn always showed the last value in a serial of plots
parts:
Hi, 

I am a beginner in R.
I am trying to make a serial of plots by comparing each column of my samples (column 3, 4, 5....) with my reference data (column 2, "Ref"). I want to draw scatterplot and show the linear regression equation of each plot. 
And save them as individual png file into a folder. However, I can get each plot with correct data points, but the equation shown on the plots are all the same. It is always the equation from my last datapoint. 


Could anyone give me any suggestion? Thank you!

Here is the code I have:

##Read data
SNPdata <- read.csv(paste(folder_name, file_name, sep =""))

## Get how many colnums (samples) in this datasheet
colnum <-ncol(SNPdata)

## Get sample names in this data sheet
colname <- colnames(SNPdata)

## Get reference frequency
ref <- SNPdata$Ref


## For each sample comparing with reference

for(i in 3:colnum) {

## Get frequency of each sample
  
sample <- SNPdata[,i]

## Dataframe of reference and sample
df <- cbind(ref, sample)
df <- data.frame(df)

## Make a plot with lm
p <- ggplot(data = df, aes(x = sample, y = ref)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se=FALSE, color="black", formula = y ~ x) +
  geom_point()


## Get the equation
lm_eqn = function(df) {
 
  m = lm(df[,1]~df[,2], df);
  eq <- substitute(italic(y) == a + b %.% italic(x)*","~~italic(r)^2~"="~r2, 
                   list(a = format(coef(m)[1], digits = 2), 
                        b = format(coef(m)[2], digits = 2), 
                        r2 = format(summary(m)$r.squared, digits = 3)))
  as.character(as.expression(eq));                 
}   
##combine the equation with the plot
## save the plot to folder
mypath <- file.path(folder_name, paste("ScatterPlotPNG_", colname[i], "_SNPFreq", ".png", sep = ""))  
png(file=mypath)    
mytitle = paste(colname[i], "_SNPFreq", sep = "")    
p1 = p + geom_text(aes(x = 0.15, y = 0.25, label = lm_eqn(df)), parse = TRUE) + labs(title = mytitle)
plot(p1)
dev.off()



}
}
